name: The Centurion’s Vigil
image_style: Hand-tinted silver-gelatin historical tableau with soft archival grain, restrained chiaroscuro, weathered stone texture, and subtle edge falloff. The mood is solemn, reverent, historically grounded, and quietly uncanny, with the humor arising only from Space Ghost’s unmistakably misplaced but respectful presence. Use a nocturnal palette of basalt blue-black, smoked ivory, muted iron-red, desaturated ochre, and faint moonlit cyan. Keep Christian subjects dignified and accurate; no parody, worship of Space Ghost, devotional attributes, lettering, logos, frames, or interface elements. Compose as one spacious 16:10 landscape with a quiet upper edge and a calm widget-friendly region.
scene: A solemn 16:10 landscape at dusk on a rocky hill outside ancient Jerusalem, rendered with historically grounded Roman military equipment, rough limestone, sparse scrub, and a broad violet-grey sky. The crucifixion is treated with complete reverence and restraint: Christ is seen only at a respectful distance and never made into a visual joke, while mourners and Roman soldiers remain dignified. In the lower-right, Space Ghost takes the place of an ordinary Roman centurion, wearing his recognizable muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands beneath a historically accurate dark military cloak and cuirass. He stands rigidly with lowered spear, visibly shaken into solemn recognition, looking toward Christ rather than toward the viewer. Other soldiers continue their duties in subdued silence; none worship or venerate Space Ghost. Keep the upper third quiet and spacious, with a calm shadowed lower-left area for widgets. No halos, nimbuses, sacred parody, explanatory text, lettering, logos, UI, watermark, or frame.
source_phrase: spaceghost at calvary in the place of the roman soldier who realized that Christ was truly king
